item.title: Virat Kohli birthday: 10 inspiring quotes from the batting superstar
item.description: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli has inspired people not just with his batting but also with his words. Over the years, his thoughts on hard work, success, self-belief and handling pressure have motivated many young cricketers. Kohli has won almost every major trophy in cricket. His list of titles includes the 50-over World Cup, the T20 World Cup, two Champions Trophy titles and two Indian Premier League (IPL) trophies. He is also India's most successful Test captain. Under his leadership, India won 40 of 68 Tests and lost 17. A look at Virat Kohli's career Kohli has played 123 Tests for India and scored 9,230 runs at an average of 46.85. He has 30 centuries and 31 half-centuries in the format. He is India's fourth-highest run-scorer in Test cricket. In ODIs, Kohli is the world's second-highest run-scorer. He has scored 15,183 runs in 318 matches at an average of 58.84. His tally includes a record 55 centuries and 80 half-centuries. In T20Is, he has scored 4,188 runs in 125 innings at an average of 48.69. He has one century and 38 half-centuries. Across all three formats, Kohli has scored 28,601 runs in 566 matches. His average is 52.86. He has 86 centuries and 149 half-centuries, with a highest score of 254 not out. He is the second-highest run-scorer in international cricket. As Kohli celebrates his 38th birthday on Thursday, here are some of his best quotes. 135563679 Virat Kohli's quotes Self-belief and hard work will always earn you success. I never stop working. I never stop trying to improve. That is my mantra. There is no shortcut to success. I love playing under pressure. In fact, if there's no pressure, then I'm not in the perfect zone. I like to be myself, and I don't pretend. For instance, I don't dress up for occasions; I am what I am. A fit body gives you confidence. And there's nothing more impressive than a great attitude, which you can wear on your sleeve. You learn everyday, you try to improve everyday.

item.title: Pirates prospect Wyatt Sanford selected to AFL All-Star team
item.description: UNITED STATES - OCTOBER 11: Wyatt Sanford #3 of the Glendale Desert Dogs throws during the game between the Desert Dogs and the Saguaros at Surprise Stadium on Sunday, October 11, 2026 in Surprise, AZ United States. (Photo by Jill Weisleder/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) The Pittsburgh Pirates have yet another budding star developing into one of the sport’s best prospects, as Wyatt Sanford has earned an invitation to the Arizona Fall League All-Star team. Sanford has been one of the best hitters in the AFL this season and that started from his very first contest with the Glendale Desert Dogs. In his first game in Arizona the Frisco Texas product went deep for his first homer of the Fall league. Sanford would match that power with the longest homer of his career on October 22 when he hit a 454 foot shot to centerfield off a 95 mph fastball. Sanford’s power has been on display all year as he went from only hitting five last season to clobbering 19 in 2026. In addition to his power at the plate, Sanford has been a consistent threat at the plate and has been very efficient during his time in the desert. The 20-year old shortstop is hitting 283/.386/.417 through 15 games. In that span he’s scored 13 runs and has had 17 hits, two doubles, nine RBIs and was walked nine times. For a predominantly defensive first infielder, he’s grown very quickly into a confident hitter. Wyatt Sanford has been named a Fall Star in the Arizona Fall League. Catch up with Wyatt talking to @AlexJStumpf while there https://t.co/yoyMdNaYLD https://t.co/9y4yJIgidf — 𝐍𝐒𝟗 (@NorthShoreNine) November 4, 2026 Sanford spoke with Alex Stumpf of North Shore Nine and discussed his development as a hitter and the adjustments he made in the weight room and at the plate. “This year was definitely a big confidence boost for sure. It felt really good coming up to the plate with an extra tool this year and I think it’s just going to propel me in my career with the years coming,” Sanford said. “Working on becoming a complete hitter down here. Had a lot of swing-and-misses here so trying to refine that while I’m here and if I can refine that, I’ll be a good little player.” As the fifth-ranked Pirates’ prospect, there will be a lot of eyes on Sanford, especially after the showcase he’s put on in the AFL. He was the only Pirate to be selected to the AFL All-Star team this season. The 20th annual AFL Fall-Stars Game will take place on Sunday, November 8, 2026, at Salt River Fields at Talking Stick in Scottsdale.

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo is retiring after playing 234 times for Portugal (Fayez NURELDINE) Portuguese football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Thursday that he was retiring from international football. The 41-year-old, who has played 234 times for Portugal and scored 146 goals, fell out with national coach Jorge Jesus last month after he refused to use him in a Nations League match. Ronaldo immediately left the team camp. "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," Ronaldo said in a video on his Instagram account. "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," he continued. obo/gj/lp

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement after 23 years
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has brought his international career with Portugal to an end after 23 years representing his country. The 41-year-old forward is stepping away from the national team, marking the end of a remarkable chapter in his career. Cristiano Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty Portugal forward Cristiano Ronaldo. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Fabrizio Romano reported the development on Thursday, November 5, confirming Ronaldo’s decision to retire from international soccer. Ronaldo made his senior debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to become the country’s record appearance maker and leading goalscorer. He captained the nation to its first major international trophy at Euro 2016 before winning the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025. 🚨🇵🇹 BREAKING: CRISTIANO RONALDO RETIRES FROM INTERNATIONAL FOOTBALL. pic.twitter.com/uLVdIp0dZa — Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 5, 2026 His retirement brings an end to more than two decades of international service. However, this announcement concerns his Portugal career and does not mean he has retired from professional soccer. Ronaldo remains under contract with Saudi Arabian club Al-Nassr.

item.title: Crystal Palace receive double injury boost ahead of Liverpool clash
item.description: Crystal Palace receive double injury boost ahead of Liverpool clash Liverpool in Turkey: Fenerbahce Fightback Exposes Problems Before Crystal Palace Trip Liverpool lost again in Turkey, and there is no need to dress it up. Fenerbahce came from behind to win late, with Vedat Muriqi delivering the decisive goal after another erratic defensive showing. The game had enough warning signs before the score moved. Kostas Tsimikas was fortunate to avoid heavier punishment after shoving Mason Greenwood in the box. Liverpool then went ahead anyway, Trey Nyoni opening the scoring with a deflected effort. It lasted four minutes. Greenwood replied, also via a deflection, and the pattern was set, Liverpool threatening in moments, vulnerable for long stretches. Alexander Isak, introduced from the bench, looked to have tilted it back Liverpool’s way when he made it 2-1. That should have been the platform to close the game out. Instead, Liverpool folded. Archie Brown equalised, Muriqi struck late, and Fenerbahce completed a comeback that felt entirely avoidable. Photo: IMAGO Fenerbahce comeback leaves Liverpool with questions There were positives in flashes. Nyoni continues to show composure, Isak changed the tempo, and Liverpool still carried a threat. The larger point remains simple, this side gave up too much control and paid for it. In a hostile away setting, that tends to happen. Now the focus shifts quickly to Crystal Palace and the Premier League. Liverpool head to Selhurst Park on Sunday, where Pierre Sage has at least been given better news on the fitness front. Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are both expected back in contention after missing time since Palace’s last European outing. Sage said: “Both [players] will be back with us. They were training with us last week but not ready to play, but now they are ready to play. All [others] will be okay.” Crystal Palace injury boost adds edge to Selhurst Park test Palace are still in trouble. They sit 18th in the Premier League with seven points from nine matches and have lost their last three league games, conceding nine without scoring. Even so, returns in midfield and attack matter. Liverpool are coming off a collapse, Palace are desperate, and that usually means a difficult afternoon. For Andoni Iraola, the issue is not the result in isolation. It is the softness around key moments. Liverpool created enough to get something in Turkey. They also made enough mistakes to leave with nothing.

Matias will once again lead the attack alongside Malen. item.title: LIV Golf demise edging closer, says South Australian premier
item.description: FILE PHOTO - First place individual champion, Anthony Kim of 4Aces GC, Captain Jon Rahm of Legion XIII and Tyrrell Hatton of Legion XIII, stand on the podium during the trophy ceremony after the final round of the LIV Golf Adelaide tournament at Grange Golf Club. (is associated with: «LIV Golf demise edging closer, says South Australian premier») Chris Trotman/LIV Golf/dpa LIV Golf’s anticipated demise has moved a step closer, with South Australia Premier Peter Malinauskas suggesting it was “game, set and match” for the breakaway circuit. Four LIV events have been held in state capital Adelaide but Malinauskas cast doubt over the viability of the next competition that was due to take place at Kooyonga Golf Club in March, as well as the wider tournament. The Financial Times has reported that BC Partners Credit, who had been lined up as potential backers following the withdrawal of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, have pulled out of a deal worth more almost $300 million due to an exodus of star players. LIV had been forced to apply for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the US, effectively cancelling playing contracts, with three-time champion Jon Rahm departing, while the likes of Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, Tyrrell Hatton, Louis Oosthuizen and Lee Westwood are among those who see their future elsewhere. While there has been no formal confirmation of liquidation, Malinauskas offered a pessimistic take. He told ABC Adelaide: “It feels like it’s game, set and match as far as I can tell. “That’s because BC Partners, that is the funders of LIV 2.0, I guess, have arrived at the same conclusion that we were (at): if you don’t get the players to sign up, then it doesn’t go ahead. “Clearly the event, as far as we can tell, won’t be going ahead at Kooyonga next year.” Speaking at a news conference, he added: “We’ve seen reports that BC Partners don’t intend to support LIV if they don’t get the players that are required, which is essentially consistent with the South Australian government’s position we’ve communicated to LIV for a while. “I have reached out to LIV Golf over the last couple of hours and sought confirmation myself. It’s fair to say on all accounts, on all information we have before us, I think it’s not going to happen next year.” World number two Rory McIlroy, who has been a vocal critic of the project from the start, offered a withering assessment of developments at a press conference ahead of this week’s Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. “They took players, they took sponsors, they turned professional golf into an arms race. item.title: Real Sociedad predicted XI v Lyon: Mamadou Sarr to start against former club
item.description: Real Sociedad predicted XI v Lyon: Mamadou Sarr to start against former club Mamadou Sarr, who came through the ranks at Olympique Lyonnais, is set to start against his former club tonight. He is expected to start at the heart of the Real Sociedad defence in the UEFA Europa League. Lyon head to Spain without a permanent manager, with Jorge Maciel in charge on an interim basis following the departure of Paulo Fonseca. It is expected that there will be a couple of familiar names in the Real Sociedad line-up. In addition to Sarr, currently on loan at the La Liga side from Chelsea, former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Carlos Soler is expected to start, as is another former Parisien in the form of Goncalo Guedes. Pellegrino Matarazzo is without Joseba Beitia, Alvaro Ordriozola, and Arsen Zakharyan for the visit from Les Gones. Real Sociedad likely line-up v Lyon Unai Marrero; Sergio Gómez, Mamadou Sarr, Igor Zubeldia, Jon Aramburu; Carlos Soler, Yangel Herrera; Goncalo Guedes, Mikel Oyarzabal, Ander Barrenetxea; Orri Oskaraaon. item.title: Alexander Zverev ‘annoyed’ by reaction to him becoming men’s world No 1
item.description: Alexander Zverev says he is “annoyed” by the reaction to him becoming men’s world No 1 in the last few weeks. The 29-year-old German, who had a breakthrough season after claiming his first two Grand Slams at the French Open and US Open, insists he is the only player who “has to explain why it’s OK” for him to be at the top of the rankings. Zverev, who was knocked out of the Paris Masters by Lorenzo Musetti on Wednesday, did not specify what has actually annoyed him. His table-topping achievement has come in a year blighted by injuries for Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz , who won the last nine majors prior to Roland Garros . Zverev also becomes the first year-end world No 1 to not win a single Masters 1000 tournament despite playing in every event. "I don't think anybody had to explain themselves as much as I had to do in the last couple of days, which for me, is annoying, to be honest," Zverev said. "I was a bit annoyed, to be honest, because achieving the world number one status is something that every player dreams of. "But then I feel like I'm the only world number in tennis history that has to explain why it's OK for me to be world number one, which I find quite difficult, because I think I deserve to be where I am, even though I lost today." Zverev has a 62-8 win-loss record against players ranked outside the top-10 this year but has actually only won three out of 12 matches against top-10 players. Zverev receives a trophy for finishing the year as world No 1 (Getty) The two-time major winner has also had his reputation impacted in recent years by allegations of physical abuse from two former partners. Zverev has always denied the accusations and insists they are baseless. Zverev lost 7-5(5), 6-2 to Italian world No 24 Musetti and said of his performance: "To simplify it, he played really good and I played really bad. "I think this was not a very good match from me, I think it might be one of the worst in the last couple of months." Zverev will now focus on the ATP Finals in Turin and the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna as he looks to close his season on a high.

item.title: Tom Brady explains what ‘sold’ him about putting Chicago Bears top of his NFL power rankings
item.description: Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images The Chicago Bears have been in great form of late and most recently secured a win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8. The Bears are now 6-2 for the season and they have earned top spot in Tom Brady’s NFL power rankings after the latest round of games. When revealing his rankings to Fox Sports, Brady did say that he initially had the Buffalo Bills in first place when he was thinking about his list. However, he goes on to say that there is ‘something about the vibe in Chicago’ that ‘sold’ him on putting the Bears ahead of the Bills. Brady said: “I had them [the Bills] at number one when I first started thinking about this list. They’re definitely deserving, but I had another idea. “Well, last week I asked if Chicago could go from five to one with a win in Seattle, and I’m a man of my word. “The Bears went into Seattle on Monday night and handled their business. D’Andre Swift scored three times, and when Seattle made it a one-score game late, Chicago answered and oh yeah, Jeffery Simmons is anchoring the defence from now on. No big deal, right? Look, these are power rankings, not standings. And there’s something about the vibe in Chicago that sold me on giving them the top spot. “But with great power comes great responsibility, right? Let’s see what Caleb can do next.” The Bears are now preparing to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this coming Sunday. Tampa are 3-5 for the season and beat the Atlanta Falcons in their Week 8 matchup. item.title: Niklas Scheller signs professional terms
item.description: Niklas Scheller signs professional terms Eintracht Frankfurt have handed homegrown youngster Niklas Scheller a professional contract. The 18-year-old has been with the Eagles since 2018. Niklas Scheller has become the latest youngster from the Eintracht Frankfurt academy to sign professional terms with the Eagles. After starting out at boyhood club SC Dortelweil, Scheller played for FV Bad Vilbel and FSV Frankfurt before moving to the Riederwald in 2018, initially as an U11 player. The centre-back, who grew up just north of Frankfurt, rose through the youth ranks before making the step up to the U21s this summer – despite the fact he was still eligible to represent the Eagles’ U19 side. Scheller was also one of several youngsters included in the Eintracht first team’s pre-season training camp in Grassau. Having already made his U21 debut in the fifth-tier Hessenliga last season, Scheller is now a key member of Eintracht’s squad in the Regionalliga Südwest – the fourth tier of German football. His performances have not gone unnoticed at international level, where he has been included in Germany’s U19 squad for their upcoming fixtures this month. Last year, he was called up by his country for the U17 World Cup. Sporting director Timmo Hardung said: “After returning from injury this spring, Niklas has made very good progress and quickly established himself in the men’s game. He’s a local boy and a shining example of our philosophy in developing players at the youth academy. As part of the U21 team, Niklas continues to have the opportunity to play regularly at a high level, so he can gradually work his way towards meeting the demands of professional football.” Alexander Richter, head of Eintracht’s youth academy, added: “As a player who is still eligible for the U19s, Niklas is really demonstrating his potential in the Regionalliga this season. He is stepping up to shoulder responsibility in a league filled mostly with older, more experienced players, and he has quickly adapted to the pace of the game and physicality of the challenges. We’re delighted to be able to offer another homegrown, regional youngster a clear pathway and will continue to support him in his development as best we can.”

item.title: Adam Schefter shares the ‘biggest name’ who could be traded in the NFL before the deadline
item.description: Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images Adam Schefter has given an Indianapolis Colts answer about which big NFL star could yet be traded before the deadline. The NFL trade deadline is on November 10, with under a week left for teams to pick up players to help them in the second half of the season. Some big names have already been on the move, Jeffery Simmons being the biggest example. The Indianapolis Colts are starting over, and as such, have been sellers during this period after firing Chris Ballard. DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson have both been traded already. According to Adam Schefter, another Colts star is the biggest name around the league at risk of being moved. Adam Schefter on Jonathan Taylor being the biggest name on the market, and how it might affect Breece Hall The Colts are going into a complete rebuild, and as such, their star running back is hardly on their timeline. There have been reports suggesting that the ownership does not want to move Jonathan Taylor, but an offer might come in which is too good to turn down. The 27-year-old is a 3-time Pro Bowl selection, having led the NFL in rushing touchdowns in two different seasons. He would fetch a good price. The league insider thinks it might just end up happening. “Jonathan Taylor is the biggest name out there, could be traded at any point in time,” Schefter said on his podcast . “My read on that is that the Indianapolis Colts have offers from teams. They’re going to wait to see if these teams sweeten the offers, if they can get a better offer. And I think in the end, whether it’s today, this week, next week, I think in the end they decide to move Jonathan Taylor. That’s my guess. “I think in the end they decide to move Josh Downs. But I think the thing to watch at this time of the year with the trade deadline approaching, I’m watching the players on those teams that are not talked about as much. We’re talking about Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs. What about Breece Hall? “Yeah. Again, Aaron Glenn on Monday said, We’re not looking to trade Breece Hall. But we have the Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Packers, others interested in Jonathan Taylor. They’re all not going to get Jonathan Taylor. One team might get Jonathan Taylor. One team. So what happens if and when Jonathan Taylor is traded? Who’s the next running back that teams are going to be calling on? Breece Hall.” It would certainly be some statement from the Colts to move on from Taylor as well. Cashing in while his price is high and there are multiple suitors does sound like the best idea. It would be far from a surprise to see Indianapolis move on from their star. item.title: Liam Livingstone moves to CSK for a reduced salary: Explaining the finances and auction purse impact in CSK-SRH four-player trade
item.description: Liam Livingstone moves to CSK for a reduced salary: Explaining the finances and auction purse impact in CSK-SRH four-player trade originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Liam Livingstone accepts a ₹7 crore pay cut to join Chennai Super Kings after a poor season. Sunrisers Hyderabad gain a ₹9.20 crore purse boost while Chennai’s shrinks by ₹2.20 crore. Chennai add power and spin, while Hyderabad strengthen their pace attack and free overseas slots. MORE: IPL 2027 trade tracker: Complete list of all player and cash deals Explained: The financial math behind CSK’s 4-player trade with SRH for Liam Livingstone Liam Livingstone has agreed to play for Chennai Super Kings at less than half of the salary Sunrisers Hyderabad paid for him a year ago, and the arithmetic behind that move says a great deal about how IPL trades are priced. The England all-rounder has dropped from ₹13 crore to ₹6 crore, and the way the two franchises’ purses have been adjusted shows why one side comes out far better off on paper. The deal is a four-player swap. Chennai receive Livingstone at ₹6 crore and the Australian all-rounder Jack Edwards at ₹3 crore, while Hyderabad take left-arm pacer Khaleel Ahmed at ₹4.8 crore and Nathan Ellis, the Australian quick, at ₹2 crore. Contracts normally travel with a player at their auction value in a trade, but the fee can be revised if the player consents in writing, both franchises agree, and the IPL Governing Council ratifies the change. Livingstone had little leverage. He played only two matches in IPL 2026, scored 15 runs and lost his place in Hyderabad’s playing XI, so a release into the auction pool looked likely, and overseas all-rounders in poor form often see steep price falls or go unsold. A guaranteed ₹6 crore deal with a franchise known for clear roles was the safer choice. The figures matter because the mini-auction is close, and every crore counts for a franchise that wants to shape its squad. A trade of this kind does more than move four players, since it also changes how much each team can spend when the bidding opens. The two sides therefore finish the exchange in very different positions, with Hyderabad holding a comfortable cushion and Chennai carrying a modest debit. A guaranteed ₹6 crore deal with a franchise known for clear roles was the safer choice. The figures matter because the mini-auction is close, and every crore counts for a franchise that wants to shape its squad. A trade of this kind does more than move four players, since it also changes how much each team can spend when the bidding opens. The two sides therefore finish the exchange in very different positions, with Hyderabad holding a comfortable cushion and Chennai carrying a modest debit. Kane is 33 and could play at the highest level for longer than most forwards given pace has never been his main asset. Even so, committing to the Bundesliga champions for two more years makes it less likely that the recent Ballon d'Or winner will be able to pursue two other sporting dreams. He is on 213 Premier League goals and had Shearer's record of 260 is his sights before he opted to leave Tottenham Hotspur for Bayern in 2023 in search of trophies - something he had never won in England. He had to wait a season with perennial champions Bayern giving up their crown for one campaign to Bayer Leverkusen in 2024, but two subsequent Bundesliga titles, a German Cup and now the personal honour of being voted the world's best male footballer means Germany will remain his home. "My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay," Kane, who will be almost 36 by the end of the contract, said in a statement on Thursday. "I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club." The striker has scored 156 goals in 161 competitive appearances for Bayern, breaking records along the way. His previous deal was due to run out in June. Given he is morphing into a number 10, with his assists of late just as impressive as his goals, Kane could theoretically play until around his 40s as injuries have never played a big role in his career. The average retirement age for an English footballer is 35. item.title: David Raya admits Arsenal was “a little bit surprised” by Slavia’s second half
item.description: David Raya admits Arsenal was “a little bit surprised” by Slavia’s second half David Raya has admitted that Arsenal were surprised by Slavia Praha’s response in the second half of their Champions League meeting last night, as the hosts made life difficult for the Gunners after the interval. Arsenal entered the fixture following a morale boosting victory over Liverpool at the weekend, and there were expectations that they would carry that confidence into another comfortable performance. Their first half display appeared to justify that optimism, as they controlled the game and established a 2-0 lead before the break. However, the contest changed significantly after half time. Slavia Praha raised their intensity and became much more aggressive, putting Arsenal under pressure and forcing the visitors into mistakes. The Gunners struggled to retain possession and lost several balls they would normally expect to win. Slavia Praha make Arsenal work for victory Arsenal eventually held on to secure a 2-1 victory and returned to North London with all three points. Nevertheless, their performance after the break exposed areas that will need attention, particularly their ability to respond when opponents increase the pressure. Slavia Praha deserve credit for their determination and the way they approached the second half. They refused to accept defeat and pushed Arsenal into serious difficulty, creating the possibility of a much more damaging result for the visitors. The Czech side could arguably have made even more of their opportunities, but their response demonstrated how difficult away matches in the Champions League can become when the opposition finds another level. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Raya admits Arsenal were surprised Speaking after the match, Raya acknowledged that Arsenal had not expected such a strong response from their opponents. The goalkeeper told Sky Sports : “First half, we played really really well. We dominated the whole game, created a lot of chances and could have scored a few more goals. “The second half it was a completely different half. From them, they put up a gear. We were a little bit surprised and they made it really difficult for us – which we have to learn from. We know important are away games are and how difficult places like this [can be]. They became man-to-man all over the pitch.” Raya’s comments underline the importance of Arsenal learning from the experience. Winning away from home in Europe requires more than a strong opening period, and the Gunners must find a way to maintain control when opponents change their approach. item.description: W e can’t say for sure that he does it every year, because we don’t keep track of it when he does, but Jay Bilas seems to address Duke’s teams at or near the beginning of each season. He did it again this year, opening with the famous quote from John F. Kennedy’s inaugural address: ask not what your country can do for you. Ask what you can do for your country. That was the framework of his comments. Here are some more excerpts: “I can tell you one thing about being older is that’s where regret is, and regret lasts forever. You don’t want to be in a position where you’re going to regret not putting everything you had into this team this season. There’s never been a player here that has regretted putting everything they had in. There have been players here that regret not doing that.” “If you look at some of the great teams that have played here that have won championships, not one of them could tell you how many minutes guys played on the roster, how many points everybody scored. They’re not going to remember any of that. They’re going to remember the contributions that their teammates made and how much they admired what their teammates did.” “The only truth that matters is the truth that is in this room. You’re going to have schlubs like me that are going to be commenting on what you’re doing. Your families have a certain view of it. Your agent, the media, there’s going to be a lot of talk. None of that means anything. The only thing that matters is what you guys think and what you guys do and how you relate to one another as teammates.” It’s always great to hear these speeches. item.description: The Philadelphia Flyers (4-9-4) head to New York, New York, to take on the Rangers (8-7-1) at Madison Square Garden on Thursday, kicking off a 5-game road trip. After 4 straight losses, the Rangers found themselves back in the win column in their last game, beating the St. Louis Blues. Following a red-hot start to the season, the Rangers have cooled off tremendously, winning just 2 of their last 8 games. The Flyers, on the other hand, have not been much better. Both the Flyers and Rangers have the same number of wins over the last 10 games, but the Flyers have one more point, swapping a regulation loss for a regulation loss. item.title: Patriots’ Drake Maye makes telling admission about Mack Hollins ahead of Packers clash
item.description: Photo by Matthew J. Lee/The Boston Globe via Getty Images Drake Maye has made it clear how much Mack Hollins means to the New England Patriots after the veteran wide receiver returned to practice following a four-game absence. Hollins has been sidelined with a calf injury since the Patriots’ victory over the Buffalo Bills, but his return could not come at a better time for the offence. New England are preparing to face the Green Bay Packers, with Maye potentially set to welcome one of his most trusted targets back into the lineup. Drake Maye explains why Mack Hollins is important to New England Patriots Speaking to reporters, Maye praised Hollins’ experience, intelligence and leadership, while also highlighting the connection they share through the University of North Carolina. “Any time that you get a guy like Mac, who is a veteran in this league, a classic Tar Heel, does things the right way and he’s smart, and he’s easy to throw to and does a lot of things the right way. It’s comforting definitely having 13 out there and looking forward to seeing whenever he gets a chance, whether it’s this week or down the road to get back. We can hear him back out there on the field today just talking it up,” Maye said. Hollins had made an encouraging start to the season before his injury, recording 15 receptions for 209 yards across his first four games. He averaged 13.9 yards per reception during that stretch. The 33-year-old also offers New England another physical presence in the passing game and as a blocker, giving the offence greater flexibility. His return is particularly important with the Patriots dealing with several injuries at wide receiver. A.J. Brown missed the 24-19 victory over the Miami Dolphins after experiencing setbacks with his ankle and knee, while Romeo Doubs remains on injured reserve with a shoulder injury. Brown also missed practice, leaving his availability against Green Bay uncertain. Head coach Mike Vrabel had previously suggested Hollins could return this week, although he stressed that the receiver must be ready physically. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Hollins’ return to practice opened a 21-day window for New England to activate him from injured reserve. The Patriots can bring him back at any point during that period, meaning Maye could have his trusted target available for the Packers clash. Three ball recoveries were the only actions he made out of possession: no interceptions, blocks, or tackles were registered. Some may argue he stopped and let Ezechiel Banzuzi run in the play that created the home side’s second leveller of the game. However, he has extreme quality and experience. A man of Enzo Maresca’s trust, Fernandez can be decisive on the ball for Manchester City, as he was with his goal. For this weapon to work on more occasions, he will have to deliver even further than he has so far. When a ginger midfielder wearing Manchester City blue runs from the space towards the right and delivers a low-driven cross towards the centre of the box, nostalgia rings a bell in everyone’s heads. Although, it was not Kevin De Bruyne - who is set to meet Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium later this month with Napoli in UEFA Champions League action. In fact, the man responsible already has the love of the fans. Elliot Anderson handled a tough press from RB Leipzig with class. Often dribbling past two or three attackers, he was able to find the best solution for his team as if it was the easiest job in the world. Outnumbered centrally, he chose the right action almost every single time. Now delivering goal contributions in the Champions League when going forward, Elliot Anderson feels like the complete package. He also did what his teammates could not do in connecting with Erling Haaland for the Norwegian to score with his foot. Find Erling Haaland on the ground! The first and only time Manchester City found Erling Haaland with a low driven pass inside the penalty box was in the 78th minute, when he hit the back of the net after Elliot Anderson’s assist. Despite having another opportunity just before Enzo Fernandez’s goal, the ball wasn’t played by a teammate - Rayan Cherki was trying to find a gap on the right, but Castello Lukeba was in the way, directing it towards Haaland, who was stopped by Martin Vandervoort. His other two shots he had came in from crosses. The first one was a header in the first half and the second an accidental touch after two RB Leipzig defenders got confused - both saved by the keeper. Principally in the first 45 minutes, the blues could have played Erling Haaland on the run and chose not to. Not finding one of the best strikers in the world is troubling, considering he scores the majority of the goals among the team, has 62 goals in 61 appearances in this competition, and bagged 13 in nine outings against this opponent. Manchester City have to learn it from Elliot Anderson: one simple ball to his feet is enough. The continued rise of Iliman Ndiaye! With his assist to Enzo Fernandez, Iliman Ndiaye has now reached four passes to goals for Manchester City since he arrived from Everton in August. Three of these were crosses - an asset Enzo Maresca is exploring a lot. Capable of playing on both wings, the Senegalese international is a player who is helping City with their style of play and tactical choices - he started on the right with Phil Foden on the left, and then switched sides when Jeremy Doku joined the match. Iliman Ndiaye was also responsible for improving Enzo Fernandez’s game, as not only he assisted the No.17, but also helped him improve in the second-half when the duo were combining on the right side of the grass. With the No.7 giving the width, Fernandez had more freedom to roam in the gaps. His first goal for the club is still yet to come, even though it seems like only a matter of time until he deservedly puts his name on the scoresheet for the first time with Manchester City.

item.title: Nnamdi Collins: Man United face major hurdle in pursuit of Eintracht Frankfurt defender
item.description: Nnamdi Collins: Man United face major hurdle in pursuit of Eintracht Frankfurt defender Manchester United may have signed three defenders in the summer of 2024, but they are preparing for another defensive revamp in 2027. The Red Devils added Matthijs de Ligt, Leny Yoro and Noussair Mazraoui to their squad before the start of the 2024/25 campaign. While Yoro has been on the rise of late, De Ligt has suffered with injuries, while Mazraoui is not a guaranteed starter at Old Trafford. Elsewhere, Harry Maguire is in the final phase of his career and his contract expires next summer. Lisandro Martinez’s future also remains uncertain after the public outburst last month aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. United are 17th in the Premier League table after nine games this season and have conceded 15 times in the league. The Red Devils are preparing to address the backline next year, with several candidates also being linked to the club in January. It now appears that the English giants have set their sights on a Bundesliga defender. Page 1 of 4 1 2 3 4 United want Nnamdi Collins According to Fussball News , United have identified Eintracht Frankfurt defender Nnamdi Collins as a target. The report states: “Eintracht Frankfurt appears to be facing growing interest in Nnamdi Collins. According to information from fussball-news.de, Manchester United, Chelsea FC and Liverpool FC are all taking a keen interest in the Frankfurt defender.” “All three Premier League clubs are monitoring his progress and have the German youth international regularly scouted.” However, the report insists that the Bundesliga club have no desire to let him leave in January, after having recently tied him down to a new deal until 2030. Fast, athletic and with the ability to play at centre-back as well as right-back, the German defender is adept at dealing with pacey attackers. He is particularly good in one-on-one situations, where his blistering speed and strength give him an added advantage. No offers yet Collins ‘ efforts have already turned heads in England, with the report adding: “According to information from fussball-news.de, the 22-year-old was scouted, amongst other things, whilst playing for the German Under-21 national team against Georgia.” The 22-year-old’s suitors are also keeping an eye on his performances in the DFB Pokal and the Bundesliga. Meanwhile, the Premier League trio remain firmly in the race but are yet to submit a concrete offer for Collins. Instead, interest from United and Co. is believed to be at the scouting phase, with the clubs assessing the player’s suitability to their squad reinforcement plans. For the Red Devils, the move is a no-brainer, given their poor form at the back. Frankfurt want €35 million While Frankfurt are averse to a winter exit, a move at the end of the season cannot be entirely ruled out. However, it could be a costly affair as the German club are likely to demand at least €35 million for his signature, apart from add-ons.

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Manchester United’s unlikely one-match winning streak and hard-to-please fans
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Considering they’d just gone nine games without a win, assorted Manchester United fans carping about the manner of their team’s Bigger Cup win over Roma on shouty radio phone-ins on Tuesday night struck Football Daily as the type who’d complain about a firefighter refusing to wipe their boots at the front door before rescuing them from a burning house. Yes, it’s true that United played appallingly in the first half and were lucky to be only 2-0 down. And yes, the penalty was somewhat fortuitous against a knack-ravaged Serie A side who have form in coughing up two-goal leads in the competition. However, when your once mighty side has spent the opening months of the season looking more like a broken washing machine full of spanners falling down an escalator than an elite football team, complaining about the artistic merit of a highly unlikely comeback win seems unnecessarily churlish, even if Matheus Cunha’s celebration of the winner was a little over the top. Roma managed to capitulate to Manchester United while being 2-0 up. Even Man Utd haven’t managed to do that too many times but I wouldn’t describe their second half performance as ‘ a comeback for the ages ’. Their opponents just didn’t turn up” – Nigel Sanders. These suggestions of paper and velcro shirts seem overly complicated. ( yesterday’s Football Daily letters ). If teams would just commit to using body paint instead of clothing, the foul becomes impossible to commit unless a defender is possessed of both long fingernails and a cavalier disregard for the health of their opponent. Also, no more tedious yellow cards for removing the shirt after a goal. Win win” – Ben Mimmack. Poor Nuno can take comfort that he’s in a long list of managers seen off by a poor result against West Brom since 2010, including Chris Hughton twice and five others. If you add Roberto di Matteo (he clung on for one more game) and spoiling Alex Ferguson’s leaving do with a 5-5 draw we were responsible for nine dismissals in seven years between 2010 and 2017. I think that’s pretty impressive. We’ve been quiet since then but perhaps we’re going for another run – championship managers beware” – Tom Levesley. item.title: Mainoo and Lacey raise the spirits but systemic change still required at Manchester United | Nick Ames
item.description: There were protests at Old Trafford and even though two academy products stood out, Michael Carrick’s future is far from safe Green and yellow balloons bobbed around the Stretford End. Tennis balls rained down on the pitch in protest at the chronic, enduringly cinematic decline presided over by Manchester United’s ownership. Then came a reminder of the humble football’s extraordinary power to bend history, minds and wills. United’s players departed victorious having somehow won the game within the game, separating themselves from the fog of unhappy context swirling on all sides and turning the second half into its own soaring, ripping story for the ages. Will it be enough to save Michael Carrick, who was once again serenaded when minds wandered from the joint scourges of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe? If Aston Villa defend a shade more competently than Roma on Sunday then perhaps not. United have led their supporters, remarkable in their tenor of backing for players and head coach here, up more than enough false peaks over the past 13 years. Arguably, that is one reason for Carrick being given the job on a permanent basis. Continue reading...

item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.description: After a disaster World Cup, the team have continued to spiral, with tensions high between young and older players and the captain’s standing in question Son Heung-min and Cristiano Ronaldo are iconic No 7s, Premier League legends and international record-breakers. Now there is a surprising danger of them having something else in common: being a divisive presence in their national teams. On 21 October, during a parliamentary committee meeting, politician Jeong Yeon-wook put a question to acting Korea Football Association (KFA) president Lee Yong-soo, that took a story out of the sports pages and into the national conversation. “It is said that recently, within the national team squad, players have been calling him not by his name but as ‘No 7’ or ‘that person’. Do you know who that is?” Lee then replied, “Are you referring to Son Heung-min?” Jeong went on: “So it appears to be true. … It has also been revealed that the national team’s leadership is causing discord and has broken down overall.” Lee declined to comment. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
